step.name: Step
step.text: Any place where work happens: a machine, a handmade bench, a check or packing.

handmade.name: Handmade step
handmade.text: A step where people do the work by hand, at one or more benches or places.

positions.name: Positions
positions.text: How many jobs a step can work on at once in a shift: its staffed benches or places, a count, never who.

team.name: Team
team.text: A group that covers several steps; together those steps cannot work on more jobs than the team has people on shift.

touchpoint.name: Touchpoint
touchpoint.text: A job passing a step: a start, finish, stop or scan, with its time.

bottleneck.name: Bottleneck
bottleneck.text: The one step (a machine, a handmade bench or a team) that limits how much the whole plant can ship. Also called the constraint.

throughput.name: Throughput
throughput.text: Money a product really brings in: sales price minus truly variable cost (mostly material).

capacity.name: Effective capacity
capacity.text: Hours a step can really produce, after breaks, stops and setups are taken off.

oee.name: OEE
oee.text: How much of the planned time a step made good parts at full speed, in %. Lost to stops, slow running and scrap.

setup.name: Setup
setup.text: Time to switch a step from one product or colour to the next. Nothing is made meanwhile.

starved.name: Starved
starved.text: The step is ready but has no work: the step before it did not deliver.

blocked.name: Blocked
blocked.text: The step has finished work but cannot pass it on: the step after it is full.

buffer.name: Buffer
buffer.text: Work waiting in front of the bottleneck, so it never runs out of work.

confidence.name: Confidence
confidence.text: How sure we are of a number: high, medium or low, based on how much data backs it.

figure.title: How this is calculated
figure.periodAll: All data in the latest import
figure.calculatedBy: Calculated by the engine from your imported data. Nothing here is typed in by hand.

formulas.data_quality_score: Start at 100. Take off twice the share of rejected rows (at most 30 points), then 15, 7 or 2 points for each high, medium or low gap. Never below 0.
formulas.record_count: The number of rows that were read and accepted.
formulas.event_period_weeks: Weeks between the first and the last event in your data.
formulas.oee_availability: Share of the planned production time the step was not stopped unplanned.
formulas.oee_performance: How fast the step ran compared with its ideal speed, while running.
formulas.oee_quality: Share of the units that were good (not scrapped at this step).
formulas.effective_capacity_h: Planned production hours, minus the share lost to unplanned stops.
formulas.task_time_median: The middle value of the measured work minutes per unit over all finished operations.
formulas.task_time_p90: The time 90% of the finished operations stayed under, in work minutes per unit.
formulas.throughput_per_unit: Sales price minus truly variable cost (mostly material).
formulas.throughput_per_constraint_min: Throughput per unit divided by the minutes the bottleneck needs per unit.
formulas.constraint_hours: A euro amount shown as hours of bottleneck time: amount ÷ throughput per bottleneck hour.
formulas.machine_state_min: Minutes of shift time the step spent in this state, rebuilt from its start, end, setup and stop events and the shift calendar.
formulas.utilisation_pct: Busy = (running + setup) ÷ the time the step was available (shift minus breaks, planned maintenance, breakdowns and time the data cannot explain) × 100.
formulas.state_share_pct: Share of shift time = minutes in this state ÷ shift minutes × 100.
formulas.setup_share_pct: Setup share = setup minutes ÷ (running + setup minutes) × 100.
formulas.down_reason_min: Minutes the step was stopped unplanned with this reason, within planned production time.
formulas.queue_time_median_min: Typical wait: half of the orders waited less than this in front of the step, half waited longer.
formulas.queue_time_p90_min: Long waits: 9 in 10 orders waited less than this in front of the step.
formulas.wip_average_units: Average number of orders waiting in front of the step, weighted by how long they waited.
formulas.wip_max_units: The most orders waiting in front of the step at one moment.
formulas.constraint_by_utilisation: The highest busy share among all steps. A step limits output when it is busy 85% of its available time or more.
formulas.constraint_by_queue: The highest average number of orders waiting in front of a step. A step limits output when at least 1 order waits there on average.
formulas.active_period_share_pct: Share of the working time in which this step was the one working longest without a pause (running, setup or a breakdown) × 100.
formulas.constraint_by_active_period: The highest share of time a step was the one working longest without a pause. It limits output at 75% or more.
formulas.idle_share_pct: Waiting share = time starved (waiting for work) + time blocked (cannot pass work on), as a share of shift time.
formulas.constraint_by_starved_blocked: The lowest waiting share among all steps. A step limits output when it waits 10% of its shift time or less.
formulas.constraint_agreement_pct: Checks that point at the answer ÷ checks run (4) × 100.
formulas.material_late_share_pct: Released orders whose material arrived after release ÷ all released orders with a material date × 100.
formulas.lost_constraint_h: Hours the bottleneck did not produce for this cause = its minutes for the cause ÷ 60.
formulas.scrap_constraint_min: Bottleneck minutes lost to scrap = units scrapped at or after the bottleneck × the bottleneck's work minutes per unit on that order.
formulas.lost_constraint_h_total: All hours the bottleneck lost = the sum of the causes (breakdowns, setups, waiting, blocked, breaks, maintenance, scrap).
formulas.throughput_per_constraint_h: Throughput per bottleneck hour = Σ (units × (sales price − truly variable cost)) ÷ Σ bottleneck work hours, over the orders the bottleneck finished in the period.
formulas.lost_throughput_eur_cents: Lost throughput = bottleneck hours lost × throughput per bottleneck hour. Every hour lost at the bottleneck is output the plant never ships.
formulas.job_throughput_per_constraint_h: Throughput per bottleneck hour without product prices = each job's value minus its material cost, spread over the job's work at the bottleneck, ÷ the bottleneck work hours. A job whose product has a price uses that price. Jobs with a forgotten scan at the bottleneck are left out.
formulas.unfinished_start_share_pct: Share of jobs started at this step whose finish was never scanned (a forgotten scan). Those jobs are left out of busy time and task times; 1% or more lowers confidence to medium, 10% or more to low.

detection.label: Your bottleneck
detection.heading: Bottleneck · {period}
detection.internal: limits your output. An hour lost here is an hour of output lost for the whole plant: this is the <bottleneck>bottleneck</bottleneck>.
detection.market: No step limits your output in this period. Every step has spare time, so the limit is demand: more orders, not more capacity, would raise output.
detection.material: No step limits your output in this period. Late material holds work back: orders wait for parts, not for a free step.
detection.howFoundHelp: We never rely on one check. Each one looks at your data differently; the more of them point at the same step, the surer the answer. Click a number to see how it is worked out.

methodHelp.utilisation: The busiest step. It limits output when it is busy 85% of its available time or more.
methodHelp.queue: The step with most orders waiting in front of it. It limits output when at least 1 order waits on average.
methodHelp.active_period: The step that is most often the one working longest without a pause. It limits output when that is so 75% of the time or more.
methodHelp.starved_blocked: The step that is least often waiting for work or unable to pass work on. It limits output when that is 10% of its shift time or less.

reason.dataGap: Confidence is lowered to medium because important data is missing. See Data quality for what to add.
reason.teamCovers: {team} is a team shared by several steps ({steps}): together they cannot work on more jobs than the team has people on shift. The team, not one bench, limits output.
reason.other: See how it is worked out below.
reason.queue_with_spare_time: Orders sometimes queued at {machine}, but it was busy only {busy}% of its available time: it still had spare time, so it did not limit output.

loss.noBottleneckTitle: No bottleneck, so no bottleneck losses

noBottleneck.market: No step limits your output: every step has spare time, so the limit is demand. Losing time at a step with spare time costs no output.
noBottleneck.material: No step limits your output: late material holds work back, so time lost at steps costs no output.

method.checks: We ran four independent checks on every step. A step is the bottleneck when most checks point at it; how many agree sets how sure we are.
method.loss: Lost hours are the hours the bottleneck did not make good output: breakdowns, setups, waiting for work, blocked, breaks, planned maintenance, and scrap of work it had already done.
method.euros: Lost euros = lost bottleneck hours × throughput per bottleneck hour. Throughput is sales price minus truly variable cost (mostly material).
method.facts: This report states facts only. Recommended actions come in a later step.
